Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Lotus Health is progressing through our security review. Attached is the CAIQ spreadsheet (tabbed) we use to map vendor assertions to our internal control families. Two asks from our compliance team:

1) We need a mapping for telemetry/observability controls that specifically call out edge inference (e.g., ephemeral KV caches on edge nodes, batched offload to regional GPUs). In the CAIQ matrix several controls reference "telemetry retention" and "log provenance" — we need statements plus one sample log extract showing request/response id correlation (redacted PII is fine).

2) We have a retention exception request for ephemeral KV cache artifacts. Lotus policy prefers 90-day retention for telemetry, but this cache is intentionally short-lived (30s–2h). Please provide: the technical rationale, current retention settings, and any compensating controls (e.g., sampling, secure wiping, access controls).

Timeline: compliance would like the mapping and artifacts within 48 business hours if possible.

Attachments: lotus_caiq_initial.xlsx (our mapping template)

Appreciate a direct contact for follow-ups — I copied our security inbox as well.

Best,
Samira Khan

Samira / Lotus security team — attached is the package we discussed. Summary of what’s included: 

1) lotus_caiq_initial_filled.xlsx — CAIQ mapping with assertion-level notes and direct links to artifacts in our drive.
2) redwood_service_diagram.pdf — small diagram showing where edge agents emit telemetry and how KV cache lifecycle is scoped to the node.
3) kvcache-retention-snapshot.txt — current TTLs, wipe-on-eviction procedure, and access control enumeration.
4) redwood_telemetry_sample.txt — sanitized trace sample with correlation IDs (PII removed).

Short answers to your two asks: 
- Telemetry mapping: The CAIQ fields you called out map to our Observability controls (O3, O5) and Runtime Isolation controls (R2). The populated sheet includes column "Redwood Assertion" with implementation notes and link to the sample log.
- Retention exception: The KV cache is intentionally ephemeral (default TTL 120s; configurable up to 2h in special deployments). Compensating controls: sampling of writebacks to long-term telemetry, RA/ACL controls (service principal only), full-disk encryption for overflow, periodic secure shred on eviction. We recommend a signed exception that documents the TTL window and compensating controls — we can provide a template if Lotus prefers.

Attachments: lotus_caiq_initial_filled.xlsx; redwood_service_diagram.pdf; kvcache-retention-snapshot.txt; redwood_telemetry_sample.txt

Next steps: if Lotus wants us to add any additional artifacts (e.g., a demo of wipe flow or a live replay of sanitized traces), we can schedule a short technical call with Mina and Jonas.

Thanks — please confirm receipt and whether the package satisfies the 48-hour ask.
